title: Weak association is detected after localization at a prime
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, M an R-module, and p a prime ideal of R. Let R_p and M_p denote localization at p [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. The following are equivalent: (1) p is minimal among the prime ideals containing the annihilator of some element of M; (2) the extended prime p R_p is minimal among the prime ideals containing the annihilator of some element of the localized module M_p; (3) M_p contains an element whose annihilator has radical p R_p.

proof.text: Assume (1), witnessed by m in M with I = Ann_R(m) and p minimal among primes containing I. For a single element m of M, Ann_{R_p}(m/1) = (Ann_R(m))R_p: the inclusion of (Ann_R(m))R_p is clear; conversely, if (r/s)(m/1)=0 in M_p, there is t outside p with t r m = 0, so tr lies in Ann_R(m) and r/s = (tr)/(ts) lies in (Ann_R(m))R_p. So the annihilator of m/1 in M_p is I R_p. By [lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization] (1), extension q -> q R_p is an inclusion-preserving bijection from the primes of R contained in p to the primes of R_p, with inverse contraction; a prime of R_p contains I R_p exactly when its contraction q contains I. Since p contains I and every prime of R between I and p equals p, the prime p R_p contains I R_p and every prime of R_p containing I R_p equals p R_p. The radical of I R_p is the intersection of the primes of R_p containing I R_p, hence equals p R_p, proving (3).

Assume (3), witnessed by x in M_p with radical of Ann_{R_p}(x) equal to p R_p. This radical is a prime ideal, hence it is minimal among the prime ideals containing Ann_{R_p}(x): any prime containing the annihilator also contains its radical, and p R_p is itself the radical. Thus (2) holds.

Assume (2), witnessed by x in M_p. Write x = m/s with m in M and s outside p. Multiplication by the unit s^{-1} identifies x with m/1 and does not change its annihilator, so p R_p is minimal among the primes containing Ann_{R_p}(m/1). For a single element m of M, Ann_{R_p}(m/1) = (Ann_R(m))R_p: the inclusion of (Ann_R(m))R_p is clear; conversely, if (r/s)(m/1)=0 in M_p, there is t outside p with t r m = 0, so tr lies in Ann_R(m) and r/s = (tr)/(ts) lies in (Ann_R(m))R_p. By [lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization] (1), primes of R_p are the q R_p with q a prime of R contained in p, q R_p contracts to q, and q R_p contains (Ann_R(m))R_p exactly when q contains Ann_R(m). Contracting p R_p shows that p contains Ann_R(m). If a prime q of R contains Ann_R(m) and is strictly contained in p, then q R_p is a prime containing Ann_{R_p}(m/1) and strictly contained in p R_p (their contractions q and p differ), contradicting minimality. Hence p is minimal among the primes containing Ann_R(m), which is (1).

lean.statement: theorem weakly_associated_atPrime_iff {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] : ((∃ m : M, p ∈ ((⊥ : Submodule R M).colon {m}).minimalPrimes) ↔ (∃ x : LocalizedModule.AtPrime p M, p.map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime p)) ∈ ((⊥ : Submodule (Localization.AtPrime p) (LocalizedModule.AtPrime p M)).colon {x}).minimalPrimes)) ∧ ((∃ x : LocalizedModule.AtPrime p M, p.map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime p)) ∈ ((⊥ : Submodule (Localization.AtPrime p) (LocalizedModule.AtPrime p M)).colon {x}).minimalPrimes) ↔ (∃ x : LocalizedModule.AtPrime p M, ((⊥ : Submodule (Localization.AtPrime p) (LocalizedModule.AtPrime p M)).colon {x}).radical = p.map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime p))))

reviewed_lean.note: CommRing R, AddCommGroup/Module M, p prime (no extra hyps); R_p=Localization.AtPrime p, M_p=LocalizedModule.AtPrime p M, pR_p=p.map algebraMap; (1) colon-{m} minimalPrimes over R, (2) same over R_p for x in M_p, (3) radical of R_p-annihilator = pR_p; (1<->2)&(2<->3); L colon convention (Ideal.WeakAss ring-only, not applicable); Mathlib-only imports; docstring = node's 3 steps
